answer: A bonded deposit protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital into escrow across a rolling commitment horizon before transacting in the peer nebula. An attacker attempting to scale counterfeit identities must cross a severe liquidity canyon, locking up scarce financial capital for every spawned instance. Although this verifiable opportunity cost deters mass impersonation, high financial friction disenfranchises resource-poor agents and risks plutocratic centralization.
